sessions.summary: Ingested CCF High Level Requirements, discovery interview transcript (briefed), EOI/Full Application forms, brand assets, and the org-wide Health Assessment. Produced the Discovery Brief covering the Community Care Fund rebuild.
friction: Org Health Assessment and EOI/Application PDFs were image-only (scanned slide exports) requiring poppler/pdftoppm install for page-image extraction.
WebSearch tool unavailable in this environment (Bedrock/Vertex policy blocks it) — research relied on central KB plus model knowledge, flagged as unverified where appropriate.

decisions.decision: Scope this engagement to the Community Care Fund rebuild only; the separate 45-finding Org Health Assessment is current-state context for design, not in-scope remediation work.
decisions.rationale: Client confirmed; the two documents are distinct workstreams from different dates with no cross-reference in the interview.
rejected: Bundling selected high-priority Health Assessment fixes into CCF scope

decisions.decision: Defined 'special project' exception policy is a client-owned decision (Rachel + Legal), not Salesforce build scope — Salesforce only provides enforcement/audit structure once the policy exists.
decisions.rationale: Client explicitly chose this framing over having Scopezilla help define the policy itself.
rejected: Treating the policy definition itself as in-scope gap analysis

decisions.decision: Treated the CCF High Level Requirements workbook as mostly as-built (current implementation) with some forward gaps (e.g. REQ-30 'Funded – Payment Held'), not a greenfield to-be spec.
decisions.rationale: Client confirmed CCF already runs on Salesforce today.
rejected: Treating HLR as a target/to-be spec requiring net-new build throughout

open_threads: Panel cadence discrepancy: interview says quarterly, EOI form says twice-yearly (March/September) — client leans toward the form being accurate but wants it flagged as a question for the coach/client to formally confirm.
Website-to-case-creation automation mechanics for the ~60% web-form intake path are undocumented.
AP-owned EFT/payment gateway platform identity is unknown.
No data migration volumes or requirements discussed yet.
No Salesforce project budget/rate has been discussed or validated (board commitment is to the CCF program itself, not a SF project budget).
PII/data-residency requirements for payment details not discussed.
Geoscape confirmed by client as the likely tool CMLs use for the 2km boundary check, but not independently verified against the CML's actual mapping tool.
next_steps: Run requirements to define epics and gap analysis for the CCF rebuild.
Consider a targeted KB/architecture query on SAP-to-Salesforce disbursement integration patterns before design.
Confirm panel cadence, payment gateway identity, and Geoscape assumption directly with Rachel Doyle.

terminology.CCF: Community Care Fund — the grant program being rebuilt
terminology.CML: Community Marketing Lead — the 4 regional staff who triage eligibility and chase applications
terminology.EOI: Expression of Interest — Stage 1 of the two-stage CCF application process
terminology.two-kilometre rule: Eligibility criterion requiring a project be within 2km of a Northwind Grid asset (substation, transmission corridor)
terminology.special project: An undocumented, Head-of-Communications-discretion exception allowing re-application within 2 years of prior funding
terminology.panel: The 11-person approval body (6 internal, 5 external) that reviews grants over $50K
terminology.DigiTech: Northwind Grid's existing Salesforce implementation partner

decision_log.decision: CCF rebuild only — Org Health Assessment findings are design context, not in-scope deliverables.
decision_log.rationale: Confirmed by client; the assessment covers the whole platform while this engagement targets one program.

decision_log.decision: 'Special project' exception policy definition is deferred to the client (Rachel + Legal); Salesforce builds enforcement/audit structure only once that policy exists.
decision_log.rationale: Client chose this over having Scopezilla help define the policy during gap analysis.
rejected: Treating policy definition as in-scope gap-analysis work
